answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the economy enforces quadratic stake burning per identity registered by an entity. Registering $N$ agents requires burning $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ cryptographic tokens, creating superlinear economic friction that exhausts attacker capital. Even if an attacker names identities after a blooming meadow, a classical sonnet, or a barren desert dune, the escalating burn penalty makes mass identity replication exponentially cost-prohibitive.
